source.value:
De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
\left[ \cos(\varphi) + \textrm{i}\sin(\varphi) \right]^n = \cos(n\varphi) + \textrm{i}\sin{(n\varphi)}.
$$

In our expression, we have $n=4$ and $\varphi=\dfrac{\theta}{10}.$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\theta }{10})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\theta }{10})]}^{4} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\theta }{10})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\theta }{10}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\theta }{5})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\theta }{5}).\end{aligned}
$$

source.value:
First, note that

$$
\dfrac{1}{\left[ \cos(\theta) +\textrm{i}\sin(\theta) \right]^2} = \left[ \cos(\theta) +\textrm{i}\sin(\theta) \right]^{-2} .
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
\left[ \cos(\varphi) + \textrm{i}\sin(\varphi) \right]^n = \cos(n\varphi) + \textrm{i}\sin{(n\varphi)}.
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-2$ and $\varphi=\theta.$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{2}} & ={[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )]}^{-2} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-2\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-2\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\cos(-\varphi) = \cos (\varphi)$ and $\sin(-\varphi) = -\sin(\varphi)$ for any input $\varphi,$ we have

$$
\cos(-2\theta) + \textrm{i}\sin(-2\theta) = \cos(2\theta) - \textrm{i}\sin{(2\theta)}.
$$

source.value:
First, note that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )]}^{4}} & ={[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )]}^{-4}.\end{aligned}
$$

For expressions involving subtraction, De Moivre's theorem states that

$$
\left[ \cos (\varphi) - \textrm{i}\sin(\varphi) \right]^n = \cos(n\varphi) - \textrm{i}\sin{(n\varphi)}.
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-4$ and $\varphi=2\theta.$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )]}^{-4} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-4\cdot 2\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-4\cdot 2\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-8\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-8\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\cos(-\varphi) = \cos (\varphi)$ and $\sin(-\varphi) = -\sin(\varphi)$ for any input $\varphi,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-8\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-8\theta ) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )-[-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta )] \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$
